name: Pointer Gestures
explanation: Any feature that relies on a multi-finger gesture, like pinch-to-zoom, or a path-based gesture, like swiping in a specific direction, must also be operable using a single-pointer action that doesn't require following a path, such as a plain tap or click on a button. The path itself is what's off-limits as the only option, not multi-touch or dragging in general; a photo viewer that only zooms via pinch needs to also offer zoom-in and zoom-out buttons, for instance. An exception applies when the gesture itself is essential to the specific function, such as a signature pad or a freehand drawing tool.
whoItAffects: People with motor disabilities affecting fine motor control may not be able to perform a precise multi-finger pinch or a smooth directional swipe reliably, even if they can tap a button accurately. People using a single-switch device or a mouth stick to operate a touchscreen physically cannot perform multi-touch gestures at all, since those require multiple simultaneous points of contact. Providing a single-tap alternative for the same function ensures the feature remains usable regardless of the input method's precision or the number of points of contact it supports.
howToTest: On a touchscreen device, find any feature that responds to a multi-finger gesture, like pinch-to-zoom, or a directional swipe, like swiping to dismiss a card or navigate a carousel. For each one, check whether the same result can also be achieved with a simple tap or click, such as a visible zoom button or a next/previous arrow, rather than only through the gesture itself. If the gesture is the only way to trigger that function, and it isn't essential to the activity (like freehand drawing), this fails.

check.question: A mobile photo gallery app lets users swipe left or right to move between photos, and this is the only way to navigate; there are no visible next/previous buttons as an alternative. Does this pass SC 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures?
choices: Yes, because swiping is a standard, widely understood gesture on touchscreens
No, because the path-based swipe gesture has no single-pointer alternative like a tap-based button
Yes, because photo galleries are exempt from this criterion
It depends only on how many photos are in the gallery
